name: pcb-e1-dock
title: PCB-E1 DOCK STRIP

finish._cont_route_why: 11 September 2026: one continuation pass of the router before the stub router when a handful of connections are open (A21's lever of 5 September). cont_route.sh keeps the board only if it improves, so it cannot make one worse; it was declared for A alone because only the A clones carried it, and E and P both ended a route at exactly one open.
finish._cont_route_planes_why: 12 September 2026: the continuation exports its own DSN, and it did so with every plane REMOVED, because finish.sh passed it no plane treatment and routeflow never put one in the finish's environment either. That makes the continuation re-route every plane pin as a wire: on C that is GND on In1, the majority of the board's connections. It is the same treatment the route itself is given in routeflow/<phase>.json, and a test holds the two in agreement.
finish._return_via_why: 15 September 2026, owner ruling 20:15 CEST (appendix 32.198): a ground via within 1.5 mm of every signal via, fine-pitch escape fans exempt; the finish places them after the last copper-changing stage and the board gate (intent_checks item 4) refuses a board with a signal via left without one.
finish._direct_close_why: 16 September 2026, E11. The board re-finished at hard 0 with ONE connection open: U13 pad 2 (GND) at (5.537, 208.400) and the GND track 1.72 mm west of it at x 3.8125, which the stub router refused as 'pad -> track, no path' at its own grid and clearance. It is a straight run of under two millimetres across free board, which is the case direct_close was written for on A24 and the case the raster search is worst at: every cell beside a target pad lies inside somebody's clearance, while the segment that closes the gap ends ON that pad, where the pad's own clearance does not apply to its own net. The limit is 4 mm rather than A's 12 because E's opens are short by construction: the long ones are the router's and they are closed by routing, not by a bar laid across the board. Outer layers only: E's In1 is a solid ground plane and In2 carries four power pours, so a closure has no business on either.
finish._via_parallel_why: 18 September 2026 (rule PI-003): after every copper-editing stage and before the ground vias, via_parallel lays parallel barrels beside any via dc_drop's solved mesh puts over IPC-2221's rating for its wall (the fabricator's 18 um plating), joined on every layer the net touches there, DRC-guarded, then re-solves and re-judges. On the committed board: E11 fails CELL_F 1.93 A against 0.74 and VIN_RAW 0.80 against 0.65

widen.why: 18 September 2026 (PI-001): E11's one density miss is CELL_F, a router conductor at 1.12 of IPC-2221's limit while the drop is 0.06 percent of 14.4 V; the pack node's own copper is the B.Cu band and the In2 pour, so the conductor over the bar is the router's, and widening it in place changes no topology

_phase_why: E17 adopted 18 September 2026 11:00 CEST: the E design with Q7's PowerPAK map corrected (SCH-005), the SENSE and SW classes, the DC_HS band on B.Cu, thermal vias in every exposed pad and C30 declared at U12 pin 6; the router landed 0 hard and one open of 94 in 19.8 minutes, direct_close closed it, the routed-board gate reads hard 0 unrouted 0, check_pcb_e 69 of 69, and the finish was refused only by rule TRN-001 (decision 31), which no route changes. Evidence re-taken as one set by gate_sweep on the frozen finished board (sha a462ac26) in /root/erf17k after routeflow's remedy round had rewritten the live tree's pre-route verdicts. Not a deliverable: promotion frozen (was E11)
_gnd_grid_why: Measured on board E, same placed board, one variable (15 September 2026, /root/eiso against /root/eiso11). WITHOUT the grid the routed board satisfies rule 2 on 90 of its 130 signal vias, 40 lacking a ground via within 1.5 mm. WITH a 2.1 mm ground-via grid laid BEFORE the route it satisfies 109 of 130, 21 lacking, and the route still closes: its winner read 11 hard of the knotting kind, which unknot cleared to 0. The grid is prevention and the return-via fixer is repair, so the grid runs first and the fixer only meets what it left.
_signal_classes_why: Rule RET-001, 16 September 2026. The return-path rule asks what a net's spectral content deserves, so every signal net needs a class and a reason. A net matched by no entry here is UNKNOWN and is judged at the STRICTEST bar, so an omission costs a failure rather than buying a pass. Patterns are shell globs over the net name without its leading slash, first match wins.

signal_classes.basis: USB 1.1 full speed at 12 Mbit/s into the RP2040's own transceiver: the bit rate is slow and the EDGES are nanoseconds, which is what the return path sees
signal_classes.rise_basis: USB 2.0 full speed: the specification's own minimum transition time, TFR/TFF 4 ns 10 to 90 percent (Table 7-9). The bit rate is 40 times slower than high speed and the edge only 8 times

signal_classes.basis: the RP2040's QSPI flash bus, clocked to 133 MHz by the chip's own ROM bootloader (RP2040 datasheet, XIP interface)
the 12 MHz crystal oscillator's drive node, a continuous periodic source and its loop is the classic emitter
the other half of the same 12 MHz oscillator loop
a converter switch node: the fastest edges on this board and its primary radiated source, so it is held to the strict criterion whatever its data rate
the LT8705A tracker's two switch nodes, as above
the tracker's bootstrap nodes, which ride on the switch nodes and carry the same edges
the tracker's top gate drives: amperes into a FET gate in nanoseconds
the tracker's bottom gate drives, as above
a bootstrap node riding on a switch node
the hot-swap FET gate: slew-limited by design, but it is a gate drive and is held to the strict bar
the fan FET's gate drive, switched by the 25 kHz PWM: a gate node with nanosecond edges
a FET gate drive
I2C at 100 or 400 kHz with an open-drain pull-up: the edge is set by the pull-up and the bus capacitance, tens to hundreds of nanoseconds
the data half of the same I2C bus
the SWD debug port, a few MHz and used only on a bench with a probe attached
the IMU's SPI chip select and its interrupt line, both driven by the RP2040 at a few MHz at most
the fan PWM at 25 kHz, a logic-level square wave with fast edges into a gate

the fan tachometer, two pulses a revolution through a pull-up: under a kilohertz, and the edge is the pull-up's RC rather than a driver's. Declared CLOCKED_DIGITAL until 16 September 2026, which contradicted this very sentence: the class is what the spectral content is, and a sub-kilohertz open-drain line pulled up by a resistor has none worth a return path. It is corrected here because the basis was already right, not because a rule was refusing the board
a counted pulse input (Geiger, DCF77): the rate is low and the edge is a comparator's, so it is treated as clocked rather than DC
the lightning sensor's interrupt: an edge into a GPIO, rare but not slow
a resistor-divider voltage monitor into an ADC input: a DC level with a filter capacitor on it
a sense line (water level, current sense): a DC or near-DC level read by an ADC or an amplifier
the water probe's excitation, a DC level through a series resistor
the cold-charge and shore inhibit, a static level through an optocoupler that changes state at most a few times a day
a reset or run input, a static level with an RC on it
a shutdown enable, a static level
a power-good flag, an open-drain static level
the RP2040 boot-select jumper, a static level read once at reset
an indicator LED's anode or cathode, a static level or a slow blink
the hot-swap controller's timer, sense and undervoltage and overvoltage set pins: RC levels and divider taps, deliberately slow
the tracker's feedback divider taps: a DC level inside the control loop, filtered
the tracker's current-sense inputs across a shunt: millivolts of DC with a filter
the tracker's current-monitor outputs, a DC level
the tracker's line-sense input, a divider tap
the tracker's error-amplifier compensation node, a capacitor and a resistor to ground
the tracker's soft-start capacitor node, a ramp of milliseconds
the tracker's frequency-setting resistor node, a DC bias
the tracker's internal LDO output, a local supply with its own decoupling
the tracker's 3.3 V LDO output, a local supply
the tracker's gate-drive supply rail, decoupled at the pin
a regulator's internal-supply decoupling node, a local supply
a chip's digital supply pin with its decoupling, a local rail
the Geiger tube's anode feed through its series resistor: a high-impedance DC bias, not a signal edge
a spare contact on the dock block, unconnected to any driver
the isolated converter's secondary-side return reference, a DC node

_annular_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, annular ring rows, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): four layers at 1 oz outer: multilayer 1 oz, recommended 0.20 mm or above. The RECOMMENDED figure is taken and not the absolute minimum, because the absolute minimum is where yield starts to suffer and this board is made five at a time with no second chance before the owner has it in his hands.
_via_ring_min_mm_why: Rule VIA-002, the VIA rows rather than the annular ring row. JLCPCB rigid PCB manufacturing capabilities, read 16 September 2026 (v2/vendor/fabricator/jlcpcb-pcb-capabilities-2026-09-16.md): minimum via diameter 0.25 mm on a minimum via hole of 0.15 mm for 2 or more layers, which leaves 0.05 mm of copper per side. The PTH annular ring row (0.20 mm) is stated for a plated COMPONENT hole and cannot bind a via, because no via at this document's own minimum could satisfy it; board D12 was refused on 16 September for a 0.45/0.20 via at 0.125 mm of ring, which is what that confusion costs.
_copper_layers_why: Four layers as built; E gets an In2 ground fill under decision 27 rather than another layer.

external_ports.why: shore and vehicle DC entry from the MIL-DTL-38999 wall receptacle
the solar input, a long outdoor lead by definition
the outside climate and ultraviolet sensor pod, through an M8 sealed receptacle on the connector plate

_external_ports_why: Rule TRN-001, 16 September 2026. A port that leaves the ENCLOSURE is a wire a person will plug something into, in the rain, having walked across a floor. Every one of them reaches a semiconductor, and the only thing between is a suppressor, a choke, a series resistor into a clamp, or nothing. Most connectors on these boards are internal (board-to-board ribbons, module sockets, fan leads inside a sealed case) and treating every J as external would refuse every board for wires that never leave it. The board knows which is which and nothing else does, so each one is named with where it goes.

GND.what: the board's ground, the reference for everything after the input filter, and the return the dock block carries to board A

GND_V.what: the VEHICLE-SIDE return, from the DC inlet through the fuse, the ideal diode and the hot-swap to the input filter. It is NOT an isolation barrier and must not be read as one: it meets GND through the second winding of the SRF1260 common-mode choke, so the two are joined at DC and separated only for common-mode current. The isolated barrier on this kit is the TRACO TEN 40 further down, and it has its own secondary
GND_V._signals_why: both are referenced across the partition on purpose and both are slow: DCIN_PGD is the LM5069's power-good going to the controller, and SHORE_INHIBIT is the opto inhibit that stops charging in the cold. Each crosses at the choke, which is the one place the two returns meet, so neither makes a loop that the partition exists to prevent

_grounds_why: 16 September 2026, rule GND-001: either the board has one ground and says so, or every partition is drawn deliberately with its crossing points named and the signals that cross listed. ground_system.py reads the netlist and compares it with this.
critical_k_why: l = t_r / (6 t_pd). ECSS-E-HB-20-07A section 6.1.2.3 works a real case where a 35 mm clock track with a 200 ps edge failed a radiated emission test: that track is ONE rise distance long (t_r / t_pd = 34.5 mm on its microstrip), which is k = 1, and the handbook calls it a textbook radiator. k = 2 is half a known failure and k = 6 is a sixth of it. The number is this project's choice; the handbook is what it was calibrated against, and no standard in this tree states a value for k

Y1.source: Abracon ABM8-272-T3, load capacitance 10 pF, read from the RP2040 hardware design guide section 2.3.1, which names this exact part and works this exact arithmetic: two 15 pF capacitors give 7.5 pF in series, the pins and tracks add about 3 pF, and 10.5 pF is close enough to the target of 10
Y1._stray_why: 3 pF, the allowance the RP2040 hardware design guide uses for the pins and tracks of a 3225 crystal beside its IC, which is the geometry every crystal on these boards has

_sense_clearance_why: BOARD E'S TWO ANA-001 FAILURES, and which of them a class could fix (17 September 2026). TRK_LSENSE runs 0.209 mm from TRK_SW2 over 2.71 mm against a declared 0.50, and WATER_SENSE 0.556 mm from TRK_SW1 over 20.49 mm against a declared 1.00. Both nets sit in class PWR, whose clearance is 0.15 mm, so the router did what it was told. Measured pad edge to pad edge before proposing a class: TRK_LSENSE's three pads are 1.760, 0.850 and 2.890 mm from the nearest other-net pad, so a 0.50 mm class WOULD escape every one of them; WATER_SENSE's are 2.000, 0.850, 0.650 and **0.200 mm at U10 pin 38**, the controller's own fine-pitch pin, so its declared 1.00 mm cannot be a class at all. What is NOT settled here is whether TRK_LSENSE should leave PWR: it lands on L1 pad 2, the tracker inductor's own terminal, so it may be carrying current rather than sensing it, and a class that narrows it to a signal width would be wrong. That is a circuit question for board E's next generation, which is also when decision 31's clamps land, and the measurement above is what it needs.

safety_lines.hazard: the shore and vehicle input is admitted when the panel would refuse it
safety_lines.why: Q8's gate is on it and its drain holds the hot-swap controller's undervoltage pin, so a high inhibits the input; R26 holds it down, which admits shore power with the panel absent. That is deliberate and it is not the cold-charge protection: the protection that matters is the pack thermistor on the charger's own JEITA input on board A, in hardware, and this line is the panel's convenience over it

_safety_lines_why: Board E reads one line of this kind, the shore inhibit, and holds it down itself. The declaration says in as many words why the de-asserted state is the safe one here: this line is a convenience and the cold-charge protection is the charger's own thermistor input on board A.
_e12_route_why: E12 (18 September 2026, /root/erf on the hub): the regenerated E design with Q7 corrected, SENSE and SW classes and FR_CLASS_CLEAR=SENSE:SW:1.0, 200 passes: routed 0 hard by the router and 4 unrouted of 94, 282 vias; the import then read annular_width 10 because pcbnew.ImportSpecctraSES leaves every via drill undefined and the class's drill took the ring off ten pre-laid 0.6/0.3 CELL_F vias (fixed at every import, ses_via_drill.py). Re-imported with the restore: hard 0, unrouted 6, the closers 3, the CELL_F widen trial kept, dc_density 4 of 4 before via_parallel, netlist_board PASS 818 (Q7 answered), check_pcb_e PASS; refused at the routed-board gate for the three opens, so E11 stays the board and E12 is the measurement. via_parallel's first form laid 39 barrels and made VIN_RAW worse (a barrel at 4.86 A against 1.05); the fixer judges its rounds by the worst barrel now. The instrument reading (ANA-001) was not taken: the finish stopped at the gate.
_e13_route_why: E13 (18 September 2026, /root/erf): E12's design with the SENSE via at 0.7/0.3, the drill restore at the import and the round-judging fixer. Round 1: 0 hard, 2 open of 94 in 11 minutes, 198 vias; closers to 1 open, /DC_HS (the LM5069 hot-swap output from the Q7/U6 cluster to the L2/C6 filter, 55 mm); round 2 (via_costs) 3 open, not finished; round 3 (260 passes) ran. The board-wide stub router fails DC_HS at 0.8 mm: the run from Q7's drain tab to the filter is the generator's to lay as locked copper, or the filter goes beside the FET. Landed 04:58 UTC: round 3 (260 passes) worse, round 1 restored, hard 0 and 2 open at the gate; not adopted.
_e14_route_why: E14 (18 September 2026, /root/erf14): E13 plus DC_HS in one locked B.Cu zone from Q7's source pads to L2 pin 1 (a 5.5 mm band east along y -97, north at x -60, 4.5 mm east into the pad; vias in Q7's pads and inside L2 pin 1). Placed board hard 0; route 0 hard, 3 open of 94, 208 vias, DC_HS closed by the band; the closers to ONE open, /USB_E6_N from J_BLK pin 10 to R30 across 173 mm of the strip, which is E7's hard net again; refused at the gate; round 2 (via_costs) running. If the rounds do not land it, E15 pre-lays the USB_E6 pair with the board-wide stub router before the route (prelay_nets), one variable.
_e15_route_why: E15 (18 September 2026, /root/erf15): E14 plus prelay_nets USB_E6_P,USB_E6_N; the pre-lay laid nothing (the block's lands are walled for the stub router) and the regenerated placement's route landed the USB leg anyway: 0 hard, 3 open of 94, 202 vias; closers to 2: /CELL_MON (222 mm) and /LTG_IRQ (208 mm), both from U10 at the east end to west-end parts; refused at the gate. E16 pre-lays the four cross-strip nets.
_e16_route_why: E16 (18 September 2026, /root/erf16): E15 with prelay_nets CELL_MON,LTG_IRQ,USB_E6_P,USB_E6_N; the pre-lay laid 0 of 6 on the empty board (the board-wide stub router is not this strip's instrument), so E16 is the design regenerated a third time: 0 hard, 4 open of 94 by the router (/E6_BST 1.5 mm, /HS_UVLO U6 pin 3 to R20, GND stubs at U13 pin 2 and U14 pin 7), all short; finish running. The cross-strip signals all routed this time. Finish: the stub router closed 1 of 4, direct_close 0 (/E6_BST 17.6 mm U12 pin 6 to C30, /HS_UVLO 24.4 mm to R20, a 1.4 mm GND stub at U14 pin 7), so 3 open after the closers against E14's 1 and E15's 2: the same design's scatter, and via_parallel took CELL_F's worst barrel 2.43 to 1.46 in two rounds.
_e17_route_why: E17 (18 September 2026, /root/erf17): the E14 design with ONE variable, C30 (the AP63205's BST to SW bootstrap capacitor) declared as U12 pin 6's decoupling so the packer seats it at the pin; /E6_BST stayed open on E7 (stub router), E14 and E16 (17.6 mm) with C30 in the PACK region's rows 17.6 mm from its pin. No pre-lay (E15's and E16's laid nothing). Judged against E14, E15, E16: 1, 2, 3 open after the closers.
_class_table_why: 18 September 2026 10:55 CEST: gen_pcb_e3.py wrote a hand-typed class table into the project file (PWR at 0.127 clearance where the API said 0.15; no SENSE, no SW), and the project file is what the DSN export and every gate read, so E12 to E17 carry their SENSE and SW nets at the Default geometry under the class NAME only (the DSN class-pair clearance still separates them by name, which is what FR_CLASS_CLEAR reads). One CLASSES table feeds both now; the next E phase is the first whose project file carries SENSE 0.7/0.3 and SW.
_e17_project_classes_why: E17's project file names SENSE and SW in its assignments while its generator's hand-typed class table (the defect of 32.224 addendum 10:50) wrote neither, so the router and the DRC used the Default geometry under those names. The two classes are written into the committed project file WITH the Default geometry (0.127 clearance, 0.25 mm, 0.6/0.3 via), which is exactly what E17 was routed and judged at: nothing the DRC enforces changed, and every assignment resolves (test_netclass). The next E phase carries the generator's own SENSE 0.7/0.3 and SW 0.15/0.8.
_ana001_instrument_why: 18 September 2026 11:35 CEST, measured on E17: the DSN carried the class-pair rule (class_class (classes SENSE,Default SW,Default) (rule (clearance 1.0000))) and Freerouting 1.9.0 still laid /TRK_LSENSE (an UNLOCKED 16.9 mm F.Cu run from (171.7, 207.7)) 0.171 mm from /TRK_SW1 over 6.36 mm outside the shared part's courtyard: the router does not honour class_class between two classes, so FR_CLASS_CLEAR is an instrument that measured and did not move the board (A45's 26 against A44's 23 is the same reading). ANA-001's answer on E and A is placement (the sense line's run kept inside the part's courtyard), a pre-laid locked run for the sense net, or a KiCad custom rule the DRC enforces after the route; not a DSN rule.
